chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Daybali narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: I heard al-Sha'abi say: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say:

In man there is a morsel of flesh; if it is sound and healthy, the rest of the body is sound and healthy through it; if it becomes sick, the rest of the body becomes sick and corrupts through it, and that is the heart.

key_terms.الْقَلْبُ: The heart, considered the center of physical health and spiritual perception
key_terms.مُضْغَةٌ: A morsel or piece of flesh, often used metaphorically for the heart or a vital organ

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the heart in Islamic prophetic tradition regarding physical and spiritual health?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Khisal establishes the heart (qalb) not merely as a physical organ but as the spiritual and cognitive center of the human being, a concept central to Shia hadith literature. The Prophet’s metaphor of the 'morsel of flesh' (mudghah) highlights the heart's role as the governing seat of faith and moral integrity, where its health determines the state of the entire body. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on inner purification (tazkiyah) as the prerequisite for outward righteousness and bodily well-being.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-109 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Daybali quoted on the authority of Abu Abdullah, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid that he heard al-Sha’abi narrated that he heard al-Nue’man ibn Bashir said that he had heard God’s Prophet (MGB) say, “
There is a delicate organ in man’s body. If it is healthy all his body is healthy. If it gets ill, it will cause the ailment of the rest of the body. That is the heart.”
